sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Irarutu language' and 'South Halmahera–West New Guinea languages' (accessed 2026-09-17)
sources.note: Nothing on stress; used only to locate Jackson 2014 handle, Voorhoeve 1989 (IRIAN 17: 107-119) and the Kamholz 2014 eScholarship URL. SHWNG page: 'Kamholz (2014) does not classify [Irarutu-Nabi] due to lack of data.'
No phonology; refs only Ethnologue 18 and Ronsumbre 2020 Ensiklopedia Suku Bangsa di Provinsi Papua Barat (Kepel Press).

sources.citation: Jackson, Jason A. J. 2014. A grammar of Irarutu, a language of West Papua, Indonesia, with historical analysis. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. xxiv+451 pp.https://hdl.handle.net/10125/100426
sources.note: Stress section 2.4.2.2 (pp. 76-77) is about Irarutu, not Kuri: 'Stress in Irarutu is not predictable.. Disyllabic words, i.e., words with two major syllables, can be either iambic, that is stressed on the final syllable (weak-strong), or trochaic, stressed on the penult (strong-weak).. The stress patterns in disyllabic words strongly suggests that stress is phonemic, i.e., lexical.' (p. 76) 'For trisyllabic and longer words, stress usually falls on the final syllable or the penult, but because stress is lexically determined, it can fall on the antepenult or the preantepenult.' (pp. 76-77). Ku…

sources.citation: Kamholz, David. 2014. Austronesians in Papua: Diversification and change in South Halmahera-West New Guinea. PhD dissertation, University of California, Berkeley.https://escholarship.org/uc/item/8zg8b1vd
sources.note: Nothing on Kuri stress. Kuri appears only in the classification discussion: 'As for Kuri, its similarity to Irarutu should not be assumed until more data is available. It has been excluded in this work due to lack of evidence.' (p. 32) with fn. 17 reporting Jackson (p.c. 2010) that Irarutu and Kuri share few basic-vocabulary items yet speakers claim mutual intelligibility. Bibliography (p. 147) lists an Anceaux n.d. notebook of grammatical notes on ten languages including Kuri, archived at KITLV Leiden (D Or. 615, inv. 326).
